# HNumberInput

> A numeric field and counter with native stepping, bounds, validation, and an explicit empty value.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.1. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HNumberInput` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-number-input>`.
- Constructor: `HearthNumberInputElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HNumberInput.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Added in v0.5.0. Empty or incomplete numeric input emits null, never NaN. The native number input owns min/max/step validity. Step buttons use native stepUp/stepDown and emit a committed change. Invalid manually entered values remain visible for validation.

## Public API

modelValue, value: number | null · label, name, hint, error: string · min, max, step: number · required, disabled, readonly: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    modelValue?: number | null;
    value?: number | null;
    label: string;
    name?: string;
    min?: number;
    max?: number;
    step?: number;
    required?: boolean;
    disabled?: boolean;
    readonly?: boolean;
    hint?: string;
    error?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ value: null, step: 1 }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(number | null), change(number | null)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        value: number | null
    ];
    change: [
        value: number | null
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, control, increment, decrement, hint

Use `hearth-number-input::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HNumberInput } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const replicas = ref<number | null>(2);
</script>

<template>
  <HNumberInput v-model="replicas" label="Replicas" name="replicas" :min="0" :max="10" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-number-input');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Replicas",
  "name": "replicas",
  "value": 2,
  "min": 0,
  "max": 10
});

element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
